chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Recognize the sign; then when you recognize him, it will not harm you whether this matter comes earlier or is delayed.”
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.”
So whoever recognizes his Imam is like one who is in the camp of al-Muntaẓar (عليه السلام).

key_terms.إِمَامَهُ: his Imam, the divinely designated leader whom one must know
key_terms.الْعَلَامَةَ: the identifying sign, referring here to the Imam who must be recognized
key_terms.الْمُنْتَظَرِ: the Awaited One, a title of the Imam awaited for the promised rise
key_terms.بِإِمَامِهِمْ: with their Imam, indicating that each people will be summoned in relation to their Imam
key_terms.فُسْطَاطِ: camp or tent, indicating closeness and alignment with the awaited Imam
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرُ: this affair, referring to the promised matter whose timing may be advanced or delayed

ai.seo_question: Why does recognizing the Imam matter even if the reappearance is delayed?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that recognizing the true Imam is the essential matter, and once that recognition is attained, delay or hastening of the promised affair does not harm the believer. It supports this meaning with the Qur’anic declaration that people will be called on the Day of Judgment with their Imam, showing the central significance of rightful Imamate.
